subject: Request: Overnight accelerant quota for Birdhouse POC (latency & throughput run)
messages:
From: Sam Cho <sam.cho@helix.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-19T18:05:00Z
Subject: POC run — overnight throughput + latency window request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team was impressed with the prefix caching behaviour and how quickly token latency tightened up when you switched to the 1-pass kernel. We have an internal validation window next Tuesday (~Nov 23) where we plan to run a concentrated latency/throughput sweep against our integration. Goal: validate sustained tail-p99 latency under a 30m steady-state at ~3.5k RPS and a 6h soak with periodic 10-minute microbursts to 6k RPS.

We are still on the free trial and will need a short-term credit uplift to cover the overnight load. Can Redwood provision a one-off promotional credit or temporary quota increase for the run? We estimate ~1.2M tokens total (mostly short prompts, 16–32 tokens per response). Attached is our load plan (birdhouse_load_plan.csv) and the scoped test plan (helix_poc_scope.pdf).

Key asks:
- Temporary quota increase or promo credit to cover the November 23 run (one-off).
- A named contact/engineer to be on-call during the window in case we hit fallback routes.
- Confirmation of which model variant you recommend for predictable tail latency at that scale.

Happy to hop on a brief call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Cho
Head of Infra, HelixAI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@helix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: POC run — overnight throughput + latency window request

Sam —

Appreciate the plan and the attachments. Looping in Marissa (sales lead) for the promotional credit/contracting side and Karthik (solutions engineer) for the technical recommendation and on-call support.

From our side we generally can offer a short-term quota boost for validation runs when there is clear success criteria and a follow-on commercial pathway (I see this is tied to HLX-POC-8921). Marissa — can you confirm the maximum one-off credit we can authorize for this stage and whether legal needs a quick SOW amendment?

Karthik — can you review the attached load plan and advise model/split suggestions. If possible, we should pin a compatible variant during the run to avoid cold-roll surprises.

I can be on-call during the window as backup. If you have any blackout windows for the test outside Nov 23, include them.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sam Cho <sam.cho@helix.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T11:03:20Z
Subject: Re: POC run — overnight throughput + latency window request

Jordan / Sam —

We can approve a promotional uplift to cover the requested window with the following guardrails:
- One-off credit equal to up to $6,000 of consumption for the Nov 23 run (covers ~1.2M tokens at the projected costs).
- Credit is conditional on HelixAI sharing the final test schedule 48h before start and agreeing to a short follow-up debrief (30m) within 3 business days.
- Promo credit will be valid only for the test dates (expires immediately after the run).

Legal does not need a full SOW for this one-off; finance will route a short promo addendum. I will send the promo approval note to finance after Jordan confirms the schedule.

Also: please ensure that the test does not access any customer PII (we can make exceptions but policy requires pre-clearance).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Sales (Trials & POCs)
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@helix.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: POC run — overnight throughput + latency window request

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the load plan — quick technical notes after a first pass:
- Recommended model: rwinf/compat-13b-q4f (balanced quantized variant) pinned to dedicated pool to avoid cross-tenant noisy neighbors. It gives the best p99 behavior in our internal runs for short outputs.
- For a 3.5k steady RPS with microbursts to 6k, we should run with: 64-token response ceiling, batching window tuned to 8–12 ms, and aggressive KV cache warmup 30 minutes ahead of the measured window.
- On-call: I can staff the first 2 hours of the run and remain available by phone if the team sees increased fallback rate. Please send the exact start time in UTC.

A couple of small asks to make the run smooth:
1) Please confirm the exact open port ranges and egress endpoints your traffic will hit (we will whitelist).
2) If you plan to use streaming, note that long-lived connections at that scale will change connection proxying behaviour; please specify streaming vs polling.

If you want, we can do a 30m dry-run the night before at 10% scale just to validate warm caches.

Best,
Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Cho <sam.cho@helix.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: POC run — overnight throughput + latency window request

Jordan / Marissa / Karthik —

Perfect, thanks all. Confirming details:
- Final run: 2027-11-23 02:00–08:00 UTC (6 hours) with steady 3.5k RPS and three 10-minute microbursts to 6k RPS at hours 1, 3, and 5.
- We will cap responses at 64 tokens and use streaming for lower client-side latency.
- We'll share the streaming endpoints and egress IP list by EOD 2027-11-21.
- We accept the $6,000 one-off credit and will schedule the 30m debrief on Nov 26.

Attachments referenced: birdhouse_load_plan.csv, helix_poc_scope.pdf (included).

Thanks for offering the dry-run — we will take you up on a 30% dry-run on Nov 22 at 23:30 UTC to ensure KV caches are primed. Karthik — can you confirm you'll be on the dry-run as well?

Sam
Sam Cho
Head of Infra, HelixAI
